summary: Sweep every league-builder/team-setup surface that writes draft inputs for two-writer, staleness, and divergence hazards; adversarially verify each claim
logs: Sweep: 39 findings, 22 unique hazards to verify, 17 verified-safe

gap.title: Club MLB identity is editable after a pool-first lock and feeds both the extraction and the live auction's CPU bidding, with no re-extract warning
gap.evidence: ArchetypePicker's disabled prop is `Boolean(setupMutationBlockMessage) || busy` (LeagueBuilderDraftSetup.tsx:4162) — never `poolEditingBlocked`/`locked`. handlePick (:2644-2661) only guards on setupCanMutate(), which only checks hasSavedDraft (:2277-2281, :1597-1599). buildPoolFirstShapeResult builds selectedArchetypes from every team's LIVE mlbArchetypeKey (:2475-2477) and passes it into extractPoolFromDemand, which uses it to compute the archetype-feasibility floors that seed the pool (poolFromDemand.ts:1773 `extractDraftPool(universe, selectedArchetypes, tier, ...)`). Separately, the live auction reads the CURRENT team record's mlbArchetypeKey to drive CPU bid targeting (LeagueBuilderAuctionDraft.tsx:561-563 `team.mlbArchetypeKey ? HISTORICAL_ARCHETYPE_BY_ID.get(...) `, consumed at :1433 `archetypeFitScorer(identityArchetype, identityTier)`).
gap.detail: Sequence: lock a pool-first pool, then change a club's MLB identity (own club or any other club — the picker isn't restricted to unlocked/human-only). The pool contents stay frozen at the old identity mix; the live auction's bidding logic picks up the NEW identity immediately. No field on the readiness panel reflects this divergence, and Start Draft stays enabled (poolReady/identitiesReady are both still true). This is the same class of bug as the capIdentity clobber JK already found, but on a different field (mlbArchetypeKey) and a different failure mode (drift, not overwrite).

gap.title: Pool quality center and pool balance preset — the shaping dials that most directly control pool composition — are not diffed at all in pool-first, and poolQualityCenter isn't captured in the basis snapshot in either mode
gap.evidence: poolQualityCenter feeds extraction in both modes: LeagueBuilderDraftSetup.tsx:2465 (design-first) and :2494 (pool-first). buildPoolExtractedBasis (:897-920) never captures poolQualityCenter — its PoolExtractedBasis fields are only cap, poolSizeMultiplier, shills, identityByTeamId, sourceLeagueIds. poolBalancePreset is pool-first-only (design-first hardcodes 'balanced' by omitting it from the options object at :2459-2469) and is plain useState('balanced') with NO persistence at all (:1461) — it silently resets to 'balanced' on every page reload.
gap.detail: In design-first mode this omission from the explicit basis diff is harmless because a SEPARATE mechanism (modeAFinalizedDisplayMismatch, see SB-6) catches poolQualityCenter drift by recomputing the whole extraction and diffing player IDs. Pool-first has no such backstop (SB-1), so a poolQualityCenter or poolBalancePreset change after a pool-first lock is completely invisible — including the poolBalancePreset reset-to-default-on-reload case, which means simply reloading the setup page after locking a non-default-preset pool silently changes the live shaping target out from under the locked pool with zero indication.
gap.dimension: STALE-BASIS coverage — draft-setup + team-editor settings vs. the poolTrailing/basisStaleLines readiness system

verdict.evidence:
All five sub-claims verified at HEAD c0a24363:

1. poolQualityCenter feeds extraction in BOTH modes: design-first buildModeAResult passes it (LeagueBuilderDraftSetup.tsx:2465), pool-first buildPoolFirstShapeResult passes both poolBalancePreset AND poolQualityCenter (:2493-2494). CONFIRMED.

2. buildPoolExtractedBasis (:897-919) returns ONLY {cap, poolSizeMultiplier, shills, identityByTeamId, sourceLeagueIds?}. Neither poolQualityCenter nor poolBalancePreset is captured. poolBasisStaleLines (:922-961) diffs only those same five fields — never quality/preset. CONFIRMED the basis snapshot is structurally incomplete for these two dials in BOTH modes.

3. poolBalancePreset is pool-first-only: design-first options object (:2459-2469) omits it (only poolQualityCenter at :2465); pool-first options (:2487-2501) include it at :2493. Its selector renders only inside the pool-first UI branch (:4457 else-branch → :4469 POOL BALANCE buttons). CONFIRMED.

4. poolBalancePreset is plain useState("balanced") (:1461) with NO load/save. setPoolBalancePreset is called ONLY from the UI click (:4481). No session/localStorage/template persistence exists (grep confirms only poolQualityCenter has load/savePoolQualityCenterFromSession at :739/:746, called at :1462-1463/:2535/:2552). So preset silently resets to "balanced" on every remount/reload. CONFIRMED.

5. Pool-first has NO staleness backstop. basisStaleLines is gated `poolMode === "design-first"` (:2050), modeAFinalizedDisplayMismatch is gated design-first (:2064-2065), designsStale is design-first (:2075) → poolTrailing = designsStale||basisStale||modeAFinalizedDisplayMismatch (:2076) is ALWAYS false in pool-first. Readiness gate explicitly skips poolTrailing for pool-first: `(poolMode === "pool-first" || (allHumanDesignsLocked && !poolTrailing))` (:2258). So a quality/preset change after a pool-first lock triggers zero indication. CONFIRMED.

Design-first is indeed backstopped: modeAReport recomputes buildModeAResult (dep on poolQualityCenter, :2471) and modeAFinalizedDisplayMismatch (:2064-2068) diffs recomputed playerIds vs displayed pool IDs, tripping poolTrailing on quality drift. The pool-first diagnostic (poolFirstManualShapeDiagnostics, :2002-2022) recomputes LIVE against the current dial — it is a display panel, not a lock-time-vs-now staleness comparison, and is never persisted.

Refutation attempts that FAILED: (a) no re-derivation at auction start neutralizes it — extraction happens only on explicit generate/re-extract via extractPoolFromDemand, not at draft start; (b) no recent lane covers it — TEAMIDGUARD is capIdentity, BOARDFIX2 is boardRankOverrides, TAXTEETH is budgets; basis snapshot code shows no quality/preset field; (c) the sequence is user-reachable — both dials are live buttons in the pool-first setup screen.
verdict.notes: Class STALE-BASIS / CONFIRMED-HAZARD is correct. Two precision points, neither an overstatement by the claim: (1) The claim correctly scopes reset-on-reload to poolBalancePreset only — poolQualityCenter IS session-persisted (:1462-1463, :2552), so it does NOT reset on reload; the claim does not wrongly say otherwise. Note the persistence is sessionStorage keyed by leagueId+poolMode, so it survives same-tab reload but not a new tab/session. (2) Severity nuance for the reader: the divergence is between the DISPLAYED shaping target/diagnostics and the LOCKED pool — the already-locked auction pool players (persisted inPoolPlayers) are NOT retroactively mutated by a post-lock dial change. The harm is the missing guardrail (user proceeds to draft believing the pool matches a setting it was not drawn with, or re-extracts into an unintended shape after a silent preset reset), not corruption of the locked pool itself. This is squarely what STALE-BASIS is defined to catch, and pool-first catches none of it. Incremental value over SB-1: even if pool-first turned basis-staleness ON, poolQualityCenter/preset still wouldn't be caught because they were never added to buildPoolExtractedBasis.

gap.title: Design-first's live recompute-and-diff net runs on a debounced 0ms timer, not synchronously with the edit
gap.evidence: The effect that recomputes modeAReport (and therefore modeAFinalizedDisplayMismatch) is `window.setTimeout(..., 0)` gated (LeagueBuilderDraftSetup.tsx:2513-2521), not a synchronous useMemo.
gap.detail: In ordinary use this is not reachable — a real Start Draft click is a separate physical user action that always occurs after the browser has processed the pending zero-delay timeout from the prior edit's render, so poolTrailing is correctly true by the time startReady is evaluated. Noting it only because it's the one place in the otherwise-solid design-first net where the safety property depends on task-queue ordering rather than being trivially synchronous — not worth fixing, just worth knowing it's there if a future refactor turns this into a programmatic/scripted flow (tests, automation) that could click faster than a human.
gap.dimension: STALE-BASIS coverage — draft-setup + team-editor settings vs. the poolTrailing/basisStaleLines readiness system

verdict.evidence: The async gating is real and load-bearing. modeAReport (hence modeAFinalizedDisplayMismatch) is set for passive edits ONLY via window.setTimeout(...,0) at LeagueBuilderDraftSetup.tsx:2514-2521 — not a synchronous useMemo. The only synchronous setModeAReport calls are inside explicit action handlers (re-extract :3037, pool-first :2922), which also realign the pool, so they leave no mismatch; a passive dial edit has no synchronous recompute path. poolTrailing = designsStale || basisStale || modeAFinalizedDisplayMismatch (:2076); the first two terms are synchronous (:2049-2055, :2069-2075) but the third is the SOLE guard for divergence classes the basis check misses: poolBasisStaleLines (:922-961) compares only cap/poolSizeMultiplier/shills/sourceLeagueIds/identity and NOT poolQualityCenter, which is a real input to buildModeAResult (:2465). poolTrailing feeds startReady (:2256-2258); handleStartDraft (:3066-3069) reads render-scoped startReady with NO click-time re-derivation, and the button is disabled={busy||!startReady} (:4677) so a stale-true window is clickable. Refutation attempts all fail: not re-derived at consumption, not covered by a synchronous check, not addressed by TEAMIDGUARD/BOARDFIX2/TAXTEETH.
verdict.notes: Class LATENT and low severity are both CORRECT — no downgrade needed, but no upgrade either. The stale window is exactly one macrotask (the queued setTimeout 0). A human's Start-Draft click is a separate pointer event in a later macrotask, always processed after the pending timer fires and re-renders, so poolTrailing is correct by the time a person can physically click. The hazard is only reachable by a programmatic/scripted flow (tests, automation) that dispatches edit-then-click within a single task. The claim's self-framing ('not worth fixing, just worth knowing; a future refactor to a programmatic/scripted flow could click faster than a human') is accurate. Concrete example of the one input that only the async term guards: changing poolQualityCenter in design-first mode is absent from poolBasisStaleLines, so during the one-render window after that dial change, modeAFinalizedDisplayMismatch is still false (stale modeAReport) and startReady is stale-true. Recommend leaving as-is; if ever hardened, the fix is to make the design-first recompute-and-diff synchronous (useMemo) rather than a debounced effect, OR add a synchronous edit-generation guard to startReady.

gap.title: A dangling team id in league.teamIds is permanently unrecoverable through the UI and hard-crashes "Duplicate League"
gap.evidence: The League editor's team-selection checklist only renders currently-live teams (`teams.map(...)`, src/src_figma/app/pages/LeagueBuilderLeagues.tsx:776-798) while the displayed 'selected' count reads straight off `formData.teamIds` seeded from the stale `league.teamIds` (line 208, 767) — there is no checkbox for an id whose team no longer exists, so the user has no way to uncheck/remove it. duplicateLeague then hard-fails on that exact condition: it maps `original.teamIds` through `getTeam(teamId)` and throws `Team not found: ${teamId}` the instant one resolves to null (src/src_figma/hooks/useLeagueBuilderData.ts:374-378). The League page's Duplicate handler swallows that throw with only `console.error` — no `setSaveError`, unlike its sibling `handleDelete` two functions above it — so the click silently no-ops from the user's perspective (src/src_figma/app/pages/LeagueBuilderLeagues.tsx:321-327 vs 306-319).
gap.detail: Once any team has ever been deleted while still a league member (see SEATS-01), that league is permanently stuck with a ghost id in teamIds AND its Duplicate League button becomes a silent dead button forever — the user gets zero feedback that anything failed. This directly answers the prompt's 'copy-league deep-copy paths' ask: the deep copy doesn't just leak draft output (see SEATS-05) — for this class of league it doesn't run at all, invisibly.

verdict.evidence: Full chain verified with file:line. (1) deleteTeam (src/utils/leagueBuilderStorage.ts:1105-1119) deletes only the GLOBAL_TEAMS record and never scrubs the id from any league.teamIds. (2) Teams-page handleDelete (src/src_figma/app/pages/LeagueBuilderTeams.tsx:664-678) guards deletion ONLY on a saved auction session (isMutationBlockedForLeagueIds at :666), not on league membership, so a league-member team is deletable -> ghost id persists. (3) No auto-heal: normalizeLeagueTemplateRecord (leagueBuilderStorage.ts:711-723) spreads ...template and does not filter teamIds against live teams; removeTeam->refresh (useLeagueBuilderData.ts:583-592) reloads through that same non-scrubbing normalizer. (4) League editor checklist renders only live teams via teams.map (LeagueBuilderLeagues.tsx:776), so no checkbox is emitted for the ghost id and toggleTeam can never remove it; count reads formData.teamIds.length (767) seeded from stale league.teamIds (208); save writes teamIds: formData.teamIds verbatim (271) re-persisting the ghost. (5) duplicateLeague throws `Team not found: ${teamId}` on first null (useLeagueBuilderData.ts:374-378), and this runs before the division check so it fires first. (6) handleDuplicate swallows with console.error only, no setSaveError (LeagueBuilderLeagues.tsx:321-327), unlike sibling handleDelete which sets it (315-318); Duplicate button wired at :550.
verdict.notes: Could not refute on any axis. Refutation attempts that failed: (a) no re-derivation at consumption — duplicateLeague consumes original.teamIds raw and getTeam returns null for the ghost; (b) no staleness/scrub covers it — neither the load normalizer nor refresh filters teamIds against live teams; (c) sequence IS user-reachable — the only delete guard is the saved-auction lock, so a league with assigned teams but no saved draft session allows deleting a member team; (d) not covered by TEAMIDGUARD (that lane is capIdentity-specific) or BOARDFIX2/TAXTEETH. Correct taxonomy class is DANGLING-REF (stale team id in persisted league state). Severity language ('permanently stuck', 'silent dead button forever') matches code behavior and is not overstated — the ghost is unremovable via the checklist and Duplicate silently dead for that league. Scope note: impact is confined to the Duplicate-League path plus a phantom in the 'N selected' count; it does not by itself corrupt an in-progress draft, so it is a moderate-severity correctness/UX bug, not a data-loss-in-active-draft bug — but the claim did not assert the latter. Verdict stands CONFIRMED, not DOWNGRADED.

gap.evidence: useSavedAuctionMutationGuard calls `getAuctionSession(leagueId, MLB_AUCTION_SEASON)` exclusively (src/src_figma/app/utils/savedAuctionMutationGuard.ts:20-53), which resolves via `createAuctionSessionId` (src/utils/leagueBuilderStorage.ts:1876-1881) — a different session id/key than the farm auction's `createFarmAuctionSessionId` (leagueBuilderStorage.ts:1683, used throughout src/src_figma/app/hooks/useFarmAuctionDraft.ts, e.g. lines 302, 412, 456, 497, 535). The guard is reused verbatim on all three edit surfaces: LeagueBuilderTeams.tsx, LeagueBuilderLeagues.tsx, LeagueBuilderPlayers.tsx.
gap.detail: A user with a Farm auction in progress (saved, not yet AUCTION_COMPLETE) can freely navigate to the Teams page and edit or delete any team — including the exact farmCapIdentity/archetype fields the live farm auction is pricing off (SEATS-03) — or to the Leagues page and add/remove teams (see SEATS-05-adjacent staleness gap) or the Players page and edit player ratings, with zero lock message, because the guard's message ('A saved auction is in progress...') was written as if it covers any draft but structurally only ever checks the MLB one. Draft Setup's own separate `hasSavedDraft` flag (LeagueBuilderDraftSetup.tsx:1546-1550) has the identical MLB-only blind spot for its own seat/owner/archetype-reassignment handlers (handleOwnerChange, handleRemoveSeat, handlePick), so the same gap exists on the page that actually writes controlledBy/gmSeatId.
gap.dimension: SEATS/TEAMS lifecycle — what breaks when teams change after draft artifacts exist (add/delete/rename after pool extraction, after board-rank-overrides exist, after a saved auction session exists), seat/human-flag changes between lock and start, run-it-back / copy-league, and GM/archetype changes post-lock.

verdict.evidence: Guard is MLB-only: useSavedAuctionMutationGuard calls getAuctionSession(leagueId, MLB_AUCTION_SEASON) (savedAuctionMutationGuard.ts:52), which resolves via createAuctionSessionId → `…::startup-auction-draft::1` (leagueBuilderStorage.ts:1876). Farm auction persists/resumes under a DISTINCT id, createFarmAuctionSessionId → `…::startup-farm-auction-draft::1` (leagueBuilderStorage.ts:1683; used in useFarmAuctionDraft.ts:302,412,456,497,535). Both season constants equal 1 (useFarmAuctionDraft.ts:49; leagueBuilderAuctionPipeline.ts:39), so ONLY the id string differs and the guard can never match a farm session. Guard is applied verbatim on all three edit surfaces: LeagueBuilderTeams.tsx:280, LeagueBuilderPlayers.tsx:234, LeagueBuilderLeagues.tsx:148 — none reference any farm session (grep for farm/createFarmAuctionSessionId on those three pages returns nothing). Farm auction is routed and user-reachable: App.tsx:401-402 (/league-builder/farm-auction-draft), navigated from Builder.tsx:917. Divergence is real, not a frozen snapshot: loadFarmAuction (useFarmAuctionDraft.ts:412-437) re-reads live leagueData.leagues/teams and rebuilds bidding teams via buildFarmAuctionTeams({getRoster, leaguePlayers}) on every resume; the no-persisted-pool branch (474+) fully regenerates the pool from live records. DraftSetup half also confirmed: hasSavedDraft set from getAuctionSession(activeLeagueId, MLB_AUCTION_SEASON) (LeagueBuilderDraftSetup.tsx:1546) → setupMutationBlockMessage (1597) → setupCanMutate() (2277) → gates handleRemoveSeat (2611) and handleOwnerChange (2629, which write controlledBy/gmSeatId). All MLB-only.
verdict.notes: CONFIRMED-HAZARD, parity gap, user-reachable. Not covered by TEAMIDGUARD (capIdentity rebuild), BOARDFIX2 (basis staleness), or TAXTEETH (budgets) — none add farm-session awareness. One honest nuance that does NOT refute: when a farm session is persisted WITH its pool (per-pick crash-safe branch, useFarmAuctionDraft.ts:439-472), already-set lot IVs come from the snapshot, so player-RATING edits don't retroactively re-price already-priced lots — so the claim's blanket 'edit player ratings' framing is slightly broad. But team add/edit/delete still leaks via the live team rebuild in BOTH branches, and the no-pool branch regenerates pricing entirely from live records. Severity holds at CONFIRMED because the guard structurally omits an entire live, routed auction surface and the generic lock message ('A saved auction is in progress') misleads the user into believing all auctions are protected. Recommended remediation scope: guard should check BOTH createAuctionSessionId and createFarmAuctionSessionId (and DraftSetup's hasSavedDraft likewise).

gap.title: The mutation guard is a UI-layer convenience check, not a storage-layer invariant
gap.evidence: savePlayer (leagueBuilderStorage.ts:1167) and saveTeam have no session/lock awareness of their own; useSavedAuctionMutationGuard is duplicated per-page (LeagueBuilderPlayers.tsx, LeagueBuilderTeams.tsx, LeagueBuilderLeagues.tsx per the import grep) rather than enforced once at the write boundary. I found no OTHER edit surface for existing MLB-pool players today — the farm startup-draft's savePlayer calls (leagueBuilderStartupFarmDraft.ts:713, :1420) write newly generated prospects into a different pool, not edits to existing MLB pool members — so this is not a currently demonstrated live bug.
gap.detail: Flagging as bounded/latent: any future write path to savePlayer/saveTeam that doesn't route through one of the three guarded pages (an import tool, a bulk-edit feature, a sync-merge path) would silently bypass all of the protection described in F5, including during an active draft.
gap.dimension: PLAYER EDITS vs the locked pool (snapshot-vs-reference across the auction pipeline)

verdict.evidence:
Every factual assertion in F7 holds at c0a24363:

1. savePlayer has zero session/lock awareness — leagueBuilderStorage.ts:1167-1213 is a pure write to the GLOBAL_PLAYERS store (readwrite tx, store.put), no auction-session lookup anywhere in the body.
2. saveTeam is likewise lock-unaware — leagueBuilderStorage.ts:1080-1103 is a pure put into GLOBAL_TEAMS, no session awareness.
3. The guard is a UI-layer React hook, not a storage invariant — savedAuctionMutationGuard.ts:20 (useSavedAuctionMutationGuard) uses useEffect/useState/useMemo and calls getAuctionSession; it returns a `blocked` flag the *page* must honor. It is imported and instantiated per-page in exactly three pages: LeagueBuilderTeams.tsx:58/280, LeagueBuilderLeagues.tsx:35/148, LeagueBuilderPlayers.tsx:51/234. The write functions themselves never consult it.
4. No other live free-edit surface to existing pool players today — the ~20 other savePlayer callers (grep) are draft-internal pipelines/seeders (leagueBuilderPoolBuilder.ts:229/260, leagueBuilderAuctionPipeline.ts:261/308/405, leagueBuilderStartupFarmDraft.ts:713/1420, franchiseInitializer, seed fixtures) that run inside controlled flows, not arbitrary user edits during a saved auction. safe.detail: Because both the manual backup/restore path and the cloud sync path move whole records as opaque blobs (IndexedDB `getAll()`/`put()`, or an untyped `data` column), `capIdentity.rawShift`, `boardRankOverrides`, `mlbArchetypeKey`, and `rosterDesign` all round-trip byte-identical through backup/restore or sync.
